response: Patient-Controlled Therapy (PCT) of breathlessness in palliative care is a feasible and acceptable therapeutic method for reducing refractory breathlessness in patients. This approach involves the administration of opioids, which has been shown to be effective in alleviating breathlessness in palliative care patients. The use of PCT allows patients to have control over their opioid administration, which can help to improve their symptoms and quality of life. Overall, PCT is a valuable therapeutic concept for opioid administration in palliative care, providing a new approach to managing breathlessness in patients with advanced illnesses.
